name: Tadalafil
route_note: Oral tablet as needed or once daily for ED/BPH; once daily for PAH; oral suspension available
originator: Glaxo Wellcome and ICOS; developed by Lilly ICOS

discovery.by: ICOS Corporation in collaboration with Glaxo Wellcome
discovery.note: A tetracyclic β-carboline derivative with a long half-life, giving a long window of action. Year is the priority date of the Glaxo patent application on tetracyclic derivatives (WO 95/19978; A. Daugan).

tagline: Long-acting PDE5 inhibitor for erectile dysfunction, BPH and pulmonary hypertension
summary: Tadalafil is a PDE5 inhibitor with a half-life of about 17.5 hours, giving effects that last up to 36 hours. It is used for erectile dysfunction, lower urinary tract symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
mechanism: Tadalafil inhibits phosphodiesterase type 5, preventing breakdown of cGMP generated by nitric oxide. In the corpus cavernosum this enhances smooth-muscle relaxation and erection during sexual stimulation.

PDE5 inhibition also relaxes smooth muscle in the prostate, bladder neck and pulmonary vasculature, explaining its benefit in BPH symptoms and PAH. It has more PDE11 and less PDE6 inhibition than sildenafil.
uses: Signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Cialis is approved in the European Union in November.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: FDA approves Cialis for erectile dysfunction.

history.title: Lilly acquires ICOS
history.detail: Eli Lilly acquires its joint-venture partner ICOS.

history.title: PAH
history.detail: FDA approves Adcirca for pulmonary arterial hypertension.

history.title: BPH
history.detail: FDA approves Cialis for benign prostatic hyperplasia, alone or with ED.

history.title: Initial combination in PAH
history.detail: AMBITION trial supports initial ambrisentan plus tadalafil; FDA adds the combination to labelling.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic tadalafil launches in the US.

pk.bioavailability: Not determined in humans; unaffected by food
pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4 to inactive catechol and glucuronide metabolites

serious: Severe hypotension with nitrates or riociguat (contraindicated)

facts: Its long half-life earned Cialis the nickname 'the weekend pill'.
Tadalafil is the only PDE5 inhibitor approved for both ED and BPH symptoms.
